best_for: Professional Go developers whose employer pays for tools, or students and open-source maintainers who qualify for a free license.

points.title: There is no free edition
points.text: JetBrains says GoLand cannot be split into free and paid tiers, so there is no Community edition. You get a 30-day trial, then a paid subscription. Prices are on JetBrains' buy page.

points.title: Who gets it free
points.text: Students, faculty members and core contributors to open-source projects can apply for free individual licenses. Everyone else pays.

points.title: EAP builds expire
points.text: Early Access builds of the next version are free and need no subscription, but each stops working 30 days after its release and may have unfixed bugs.

points.title: Already paying for IntelliJ?
points.text: The Go plugin for IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate has the same core Go features. GoLand adds prebuilt indexes for the Go SDK and keeps Go settings at the top level, so it feels tidier if Go is all you write.

points.title: Windows: per-user or machine-wide
points.text: Installers are offered for x64 and Arm64, each in a per-user and an all-users form. The per-user one does not need administrator rights.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is unofficial
points.text: The Flatpak for x64 and Arm64 is a community package that Flathub says is not affiliated with JetBrains. To use a system Go inside its sandbox, point GOROOT at a path under `/var/run/host`.

points.title: Old releases kept for Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 91 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
